ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance screening of all partners, UBOs, directors, and the corporate general partner against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List and UN sanctions implemented under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (iii) the OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, given the use of USD payment rails via PayPal and Wise; (iv) the EU and UK (HMT) consolidated sanctions lists; (v) FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs), foreign and domestic; and (vi) adverse media and regulatory enforcement records. Screening results must be documented, retained for at least five years per FINTRAC record-keeping rules, and refreshed at onboarding and periodically on a risk-based schedule.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca) and BC Registry Services (bcregistry.gov.bc.ca); a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) national search is mandatory and is submitted through an accredited search house.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC limited partnership name must include the words 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.' or 'LP'; French equivalents ('société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.') are accepted. Names may be expressed in English, French, or a combination, using Latin script, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation; non-Latin script names must be accompanied by a transliterated Latin-script rendering. The name must be distinct and must not mislead as to the nature, quality, or jurisdiction of the business (Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, Part 2 and associated registry policies).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the NUANS-based name request is rejected, the applicant or its BC-registered agent may file a written reconsideration request with the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the notice, presenting evidence of distinctiveness, prior coexistence in the NUANS database, consent letters, and legal argument; if the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241. A name reservation may be renewed for one additional 56-day period before the LP registration must be completed or the name is released.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. The Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c 62, requires a registered office and registered agent with a physical street address inside British Columbia; a mail-forwarding-only address or pure virtual office without a physical presence is not compliant for registry purposes. Service-provider office addresses are accepted, but for this SaaS market-research model, the LP should maintain economic substance in Canada, including a Canadian bank account, operational records, and active management of the platform, to avoid CRA anti-avoidance challenges under section 247 of the Income Tax Act and to satisfy PayPal and Wise commercial onboarding policies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate. Approximately 3% likelihood of unannounced registry compliance inspection at the service-provider address within the first year; approximately 12% likelihood of a CRA commercial-substance audit within the first three years for a cross-border revenue-routing LP; the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier keeps the FINTRAC examination probability below 5% annually.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The declaration must state the agreed initial capital contribution; contributions of cash or property are due under the limited partnership agreement and need not be escrowed unless the agreement or investors require it.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the limited partnership adopt the partnership agreement and accept capital contributions from initial limited partners for a consumer panel survey and market research platform. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be maintained at the address in the Declaration of Limited Partnership and that a registered records agent be appointed. FURTHER RESOLVED that the designated individuals be appointed as officers of the general partner with authority to execute contracts, open payment accounts (PayPal Mass Payout and Wise), file tax returns, and manage compliance. RESOLVED FURTHER that the general partner take all steps to obtain registrations and any required municipal business licence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Online (Name Request module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation for the proposed limited partnership through Corporate Online, using a NUANS-style search to confirm availability. Include 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' if required. Payment of the name reservation fee is made at submission.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name (and alternate names)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised Name Request within the registry notice period or request administrative reconsideration with supporting trade-mark/consent evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and each general partner; notarization not mandatory in BC if electronic signature requirements are met
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Declaration of Limited Partnership containing the partnership name, registered office address, full name and address of each general partner, prescribed statement of liability, and any restrictions on partnership business. Execute the declaration by all general partners in accordance with the Partnership Act.
required_dossiers: Consents of each general and limited partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies incomplete or inconsistent statements, amend and re-execute the declaration and refile through Corporate Online within the specified correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration and Obtain Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Online (Filing and Payment portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership, pay the prescribed filing fee, and receive the Certificate of Limited Partnership. Review the returned filed declaration for any registry-imposed conditions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, respond to the Notice of Registry Query within 14 days with corrective answers or amended schedules; failure to respond may require a fresh declaration and new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services and registered records agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office is a physical address in British Columbia where notices may be served. Appoint a registered records agent if desired and file the appointment with the registry. Maintain partnership records at the registered office or another BC address as stated in records.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office or consent form
Appointment of registered records agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the office notice, file an updated Notice of Change of Registered Office with the correct address and confirm service details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Business Number and Tax Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance (Provincial Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Limited Partnership to register for a federal Business Number (BN), and open CRA program accounts for GST/HST, payroll, and income tax as applicable. Register for BC PST account if the platform supplies taxable goods/services in BC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA returns a data validation error, call the CRA Business Window with the error code and provide the certificate and an officer declaration to resolve the issue.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable—office-based SaaS operations produce no point-source wastewater, VOC emissions, or regulated air discharges; any e-waste must be handled under the BC Recycling Regulation and applicable municipal guidelines

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business-business-number-registration.html); for provincial sales tax, BC Ministry of Finance – eTaxBC (https://etax.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A British Columbia Limited Partnership (BC LP) obtains a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA through Business Registration Online or, for non-resident applicants, by filing Form RC176 or equivalent. The applicant must supply the LP's constituent documents (registration statement, partnership agreement), identify a representative/resident agent if the LP has no Canadian residence, and elect the desired statutory accounts: RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll), RM (import/export). A GST/HST account (RT) is mandatory if the LP's gross taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a trailing 12-month period or if it engages in commercial activity in Canada. For BC PST, registration must be completed through eTaxBC once the LP makes taxable sales of goods or services in British Columbia; an in-province agent may be required for non-resident registrants.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canadian federal or BC provincial income tax law. A BC LP is fiscally transparent under ITA section 96; the partnership files an information return (T5013) but is not taxed as a separate entity. Available elections include: (i) ETA subsection 273(1) qualifying-partnership election to treat one designated member as the registrant for GST/HST purposes in respect of partnership supplies; (ii) ITA section 216 election for non-resident partners to report and be taxed on net Canadian-source rental or logging income; (iii) GST/HST quick method and streamlined accounting elections if eligibility thresholds are met; (iv) tax treaty transparent-entity elections/look-through notifications where applicable, including hybrid mismatch coordination under the Canada-US treaty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Excise Tax Act; British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) under the BC Provincial Sales Tax Act. BC is a non-participating province, so no Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applies; the standard GST rate in BC is 5%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in worldwide gross taxable supplies (trailing 12-month period) triggers mandatory registration. BC PST: registration is required for sellers making taxable sales in BC, subject to the small-seller exemption for aggregate taxable sales of CAD 50,000 or less in the preceding 12 months; this exemption does not apply to services that are prescribed PST-taxable and is subject to current BC law.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no national e-invoicing API requirement, and no digital stamping regime applies in Canada or BC. B2B and B2C invoices may be issued in paper or electronic format. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via CRA My Business Account or GST/HST NETFILE. The pan-Canadian PEPPOL BIS 3.0 framework is available on a voluntary basis for B2G e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may zero-rate a supply of market research / consumer panel survey platform services under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act if the supply is made to a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST, the service is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, and the service is not otherwise rendered to an individual physically present in Canada at the time the service is performed. CRA administrative practice requires documentation sufficient to show that the recipient is non-resident and that the supply is an export (e.g., contract, invoices, payment instructions, and evidence that the service's initiative or target audience is outside Canada).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed service agreement with the non-resident client identifying the recipient and terms
Commercial invoices and periodic service/usage reports evidencing that market-research deliverables were performed and supplied outside Canada
Non-residency evidence for the purchaser, such as W-8 forms, foreign registry extract, or equivalent self-declaration
Bank remittance records or payment confirmations from PayPal Mass Payout / Wise showing foreign-source payment in CAD or FX
Internal GST/HST zero-rating worksheet referencing the applicable Schedule VI, Part V provision and the CRA file number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period (or longer in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud) and reverse zero-ratings, assess GST at 5%, charge arrears interest, and apply penalties. ETA subsection 285.1 imposes up to a 25% false-statement penalty on net tax misreported; ITA section 163(2) provides a 50% gross-negligence penalty on income misstatements; intentional evasion may lead to criminal prosecution and fines under the Criminal Code or the Excise Tax Act. Retroactive clawbacks are limited by the applicable statutory assessment window unless the taxpayer waives it.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and payments-systems authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential supervisor of federally regulated banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/ATF and cross-border EFT reporting authority. Canada does not operate a dedicated foreign-exchange control administration equivalent to an exchange-control bureau; foreign-exchange policy is effected through the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and OSFI/FINTRAC compliance requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account currency convertibility consistent with IMF Article VIII obligations. There are no exchange-control approvals for inward or outward transfers, and the Canadian dollar trades freely. Profit remittances by a British Columbia Limited Partnership to non-resident limited partners are legally unrestricted at the FX level. The only structural hurdles are tax-related: a non-resident partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP is generally taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada) on its share of Canadian-source business income and must file a Canadian return; if profit allocations are instead characterized as distributions not attributable to a permanent establishment, careful treaty analysis and, where applicable, Part XIII withholding or a section 216 election apply. Anti-money-laundering record-keeping and FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting are the only prudential friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no prescribed conversion ratio exists in Canada. Exporters and cross-border service providers, including the LP, may retain export earnings in any convertible currency and repatriate or disburse them freely. However, under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, every international electronic funds transfer (IEFT) of C$10,000 or more in a single transaction is reportable by the financial institution to FINTRAC, and the underlying payment documentation must include the originator, beneficiary, and transaction purpose to evidence the commercial export of market-research services.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payoneer, Currenxie) used as payout-facilitation rails; Low as a primary depository or capital-escrow provider. Legal constraints: offshore EMIs are not authorized deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act (Canada); they may operate as Money Service Businesses or foreign payment-service providers and, if servicing Canadian clients, generally require FINTRAC MSB registration unless a network/relaxation applies. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act, payment services that are not deposit-taking are subject to registration and oversight by the Bank of Canada when in force. Consequently, the BC Limited Partnership should maintain its principal treasury and capital escrow with a Canadian Schedule I bank for CDIC-insured deposits, BC registry credibility, and investor protection, while using FINTRAC-registered EMIs solely for low-value cross-border mass payouts to consumer panelists and survey respondents (e.g., PayPal Mass Payout, Wise Batch).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Policy-dependent, but predominantly physical or live-video authenticated. The PCMLTFA does not statutorily mandate an in-branch interview for a corporate/partnership client; however, Canadian Schedule I banks uniformly require the general partner and at least one authorized signatory (Canadian-resident preferred) to complete an in-person or supervised video KYC identity verification before activating cross-border or multi-currency accounts. A fully remote opening is possible only for a Low-Risk Standard entity, provided the bank receives notarized passport scans of all signatories, a certified British Columbia Limited Partnership registration extract issued through BC Corporate Online, the full limited partnership agreement, an individual-with-significant-control register, and source-of-funds declarations for every capital contributor. Physical presence is near-mandatory for the Capital Escrow Account; directors or general partners may satisfy this at a Vancouver/Toronto/Calgary branch, and non-resident limited partners must not be named signatories without a Canadian-resident agent or general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of the Limited Partnership (unregistered limited partners, trust-held LP interests, or multi-layered capital contribution chain).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: BC Registry Individual with Significant Control register; executed LP agreement with full capitalization schedule and capital-call notices; corporate authorization resolution by the general partner appointing the account signatories; identity documents and bank references for every limited partner; a tiered CDC chart evidencing the source of contributed funds; and an OSFI-aligned beneficial-ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners or capital sourced from jurisdictions perceived as high-risk or tax-haven jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: valid passports and tax identification numbers of each non-resident limited partner; independent corporate registry extracts (apostilled or notarized) for corporate partners; audited source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters; commercial-substance evidence consisting of the market-research platform's client contracts, ISIC 7320/NAICS 541910 description, and projected revenue model; and a written commitment to file the LP's Canadian Part I income and information returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mass-payout engine to consumer panelists and survey respondents may be classified as unlicensed money transmission or a designated money-services business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: executed panelist participation agreements with fair-market-value incentive schedules; AML and sanctions screening of all payee lists; a documented legal memorandum concluding the platform is engaged in payment facilitation rather than money transmission; transaction-monitoring procedures reconciling survey completions to payouts; FINTRAC MSB registration if any incidental transmission activity arises; and a segregated 'consumer incentivization' ledger available to the bank on demand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominal physical office footprint and absence of a mandatory statutory licence, which some banks treat as higher-velocity or substance-risk signals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: British Columbia office lease or co-working licence; registered agent confirmation; audited or management-reviewed financial forecasts; evidence of prior personal/business banking history of the directors; platform terms of service, privacy policy, and data-processing agreements; and a low-risk categorization memo endorsed by the bank's compliance unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) non-resident limited partners initiate a SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS for USD) to the LP's Schedule I bank account in British Columbia, quoting the exact beneficiary name and BC LP registration number in the beneficiary field; (2) the remittance information narrative should state 'LP capital contribution - BC registry [CA_BC entity identifier]' to facilitate Canadian balance-of-payments coding as direct investment/equity, as Canada does not mandate a numeric FX purpose code; (3) the receiving bank must report any international EFT of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC and will retain an originator/beneficiary record; (4) the treasury team must retain the capital-call notice, signed subscription documents, passports/tax IDs of the remitting partners, and the originating bank statement to substantiate the source of funds; (5) the CAD-denominated domestic leg settles via Payments Canada Lynx high-value system; USD legs settle through the bank's U.S. correspondent and are converted at prevailing market rates or under a pre-agreed forward; (6) the bank's credit advice should be filed to the LP's capital ledger to support future Part I/treaty filings and any capital-account attribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) high-value vendor settlements and fieldwork-procurement invoices are paid by SWIFT MT103 / ISO 20022 pain.001 through the Canadian clearing network (Lynx for CAD; U.S. correspondent rails for USD); (2) Commercial Letters of Credit are generally inapplicable to a SaaS consumer-panel platform; the standard is open-account settlement, with an LC or bank guarantee reserved only for large fieldwork or data-procurement contracts where counterparties require trade finance collateral; (3) low-value mass payouts to consumer panelists are executed via PayPal Mass Payout API and Wise Business batch rails, pre-funded through a dual-currency CAD/USD treasury corridor at the main bank; (4) each outbound international EFT of C$10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC as an IETF report; (5) all payees and counterparties are screened against Global Affairs Canada, OSFI, and international sanctions lists; (6) a stand-alone 'client incentive' ledger must reconcile every payout to a survey-completion event, and the bank should be given monthly aggregation reports to preserve the Low_Risk_Standard AML classification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (outright, tenors up to 12 months) with a Canadian Schedule I bank counterparty under an ISDA 2002 / CSA master agreement, used to lock CAD/USD conversion of survey-revenue receipts and panelist-payout exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-convertibility or thin-liquidity currencies (e.g., offshore CNY, INR, IDR, PHP, VND) where onshore deliverable liquidity is not accessible for mass-payout funding.
Cross-currency swaps and FX swap/rollover transactions to manage CAD/USD/EUR working-capital corridor mismatches across the LP's market-research hubs without speculative positions.

Purchased European FX options (plain vanilla, premium-paying) to cap downside on large multi-country survey or tender rollouts while preserving upside, with no sold-option or exotic structure permitted under the LP's hedging policy.
Bank-provided automatic hedging sweeps on the operational multi-currency account, converting excess USD/EUR balances into CAD at pre-set thresholds to minimize unhedged net exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Report (Partnership Act, Part 5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Registry, Government of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months of each anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 (approx. USD 74) per overdue year; failure to file 2 consecutive annual reports permits the Registrar to strike the LP off the register and dissolve it administratively; general partners remain jointly and severally liable for obligations accrued during the delinquency period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal) with British Columbia provincial partnership schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Government of British Columbia via T5013 provincial data schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the fiscal year-end for a December 31 partnership year; otherwise the last day of the month following 3 months after the partnership fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA penalty under the Income Tax Act of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100; maximum CAD 2,500) for late or omitted T5013; partners remain liable for tax on allocated income.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return and reconciliation (applicable to the survey platform's taxable supplies and incentive disbursements if the LP is registered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 month after the end of each GST/HST reporting period; 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual electronic filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA prescribed-rate daily interest plus late-filing penalty under the Excise Tax Act of 1% of net tax owing with 25% of that base amount added per full month of delinquency, capped at 12 months.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under BC law. The Partnership Act (Part 5) does not impose a statutory audit or review engagement on limited partnerships, and the Business Corporations Act audit thresholds are inapplicable to LPs. An audit may be triggered by the partnership agreement, lender covenants, investor requirements, or a CRA demand.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook, Part II) is the default GAAP for a private Canadian limited partnership; IFRS is permitted, and becomes mandatory if the LP is publicly accountable as defined in the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing is required for BC limited partnerships. The BC annual report records only the partnership name, registered office, and general partners; limited partners are not listed on the public registry record. Transfers of partnership interests do not require registry filings, but changes in general partners or registered office particulars trigger an amended declaration or notice to the Registrar within the prescribed period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited partner names, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, admission and transfer records)
Governance Record and Minute Book (partnership agreement, consents, and resolutions of the general partner and partners)
Books and Accounting Records maintained at the BC registered office or at a designated location in Canada under Income Tax Act section 230

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 190–590 per year (CAD 260–800) for commercial registered office and annual corporate agent representation in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required; market estimate USD 1,100–3,700 (CAD 1,500–5,000) for a CPA review engagement and USD 3,700–7,400 (CAD 5,000–10,000) for a full audit of a small private LP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the LP entity level (flow-through under ITA s.96); combined general corporate rate of 27% (15% federal + 12% BC) applies to corporate partners on allocated income; individual partners taxed at progressive Canadian federal and BC rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday for market-research SaaS. Partner-level incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction reducing the combined rate to 11% (federal 9% + BC 2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; refundable SR&ED investment tax credit of 35% for CCPC partners (15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs); BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit of 17.5% refundable only for qualifying interactive digital media products (verify eligibility for the survey platform).
